result.killer: No decisive killer. Partial: the RZS registration deadline passed around 31 Dec 2025 (Art. 66(5)). Incumbent manager software with co-owner portals exists (the mSuvlasnik iOS app; vendor name unverified).
result.reason: Not refuted by a named killer, but the idea is weaker than the claim says. The consolidated law (Art. 66(5)) gave managers 6 months after the registers were set up to file RZS entries, so about 31 Dec 2025. That one-off rush is over, and what's left is filing within 90 days when a new building is taken over (Art. 10(6)). The 1 Jan 2027 deadline for new contracts is confirmed (Art. 61(1)), but it falls in under 3 months and is mostly legal templating. NN 47/26 is only a correction. Constitutional Court challenges failed in March and July 2026. Manager-side software already exists: mSuvlasnik is a Croatian co-owner app tied to the manager's web portal, though its developer is unverified. OSS bulk upload and the number of managers were not reached.

result.killer: None found. The partial substitutes are service providers (Manpower Croatia, EOR platforms like Deel and Gloroots), generic expiry-tracking HR modules (Odoo hr-employee-documents-expiry), and the state filing tools (HZZ platform, MUP Burza rada app), which do not track ongoing compliance.
result.reason: I ran seven searches, in Croatian and English, and found nothing that kills this. No Croatian product tracks foreign workers' permits, expiry dates or 2026-law duties. The state tools only handle filing: the HZZ online platform covers 90-day seasonal permits, and other requests go to the police by e-mail. Status tracking was only planned. The market is real: MUP issued 94,113 permits in H1 2026 (36,601 renewals), mostly in tourism and construction. I could not find how many employers that is. Score stays modest because three things already cover the job: agencies, lawyers and EOR firms (Manpower, Deel) do permit work as a service; generic document-expiry modules exist (Odoo add-on); and the workflow is mostly reminders plus checklists.

result.competitor: No Croatian tool for tracking permits or expiry dates was found in three searches. Foreign products exist (HRappka in Poland, SAP SuccessFactors Visa & Permits, Pandahrms). The state HZZ/MUP application covers filing, but news reports say it is buggy and has no status tracking. Employment agencies, lawyers and accountants do the core permit work as a service. Croatian payroll and HR vendors (e.g. modules for workers' records) were not checked one by one, so there is a risk this is a generic HR-document feature.
result.duty: Zakon o strancima as amended by NN 55/26 (in force 4.6.2026). Only an employer that actively carries out the registered business tied to the job can get a permit. A worker hired after a labour-market test may work only in that police district. Change of employer is allowed after 6 months. Under Art. 95, the employer must notify police within 15 days when the contract or another permit condition ends. Fine for a legal person under Art. 251: 660-920 EUR, plus 60-390 EUR for the responsible person, as cited in Varaždin court decisions. Courts have often prosecuted this. Seasonal permits must be renewed at least 15 days before expiry. Under the workers' records rulebook (Pravilnik o evidencijama o radnicima), the permit or work registration certificate is a mandatory field. Corrections to the claim: the A1.1 exam obligation is postponed to 4.6.2027. The 30-day board-member rule and the 5,000-20,000 EUR fines were not verified.
result.market: MUP 2024: 172,499 residence and work permits (68,912 construction, 45,868 tourism and hospitality). About 117,549 foreign workers held valid permits at the end of 2024. MUP: 213k applications by October 2025. HUP expects more than 200k foreign workers. The number of employers is not published; it is likely in the low tens of thousands (estimate, not verified).
result.reason: The duty is real. NN 55/26 has been in force since 4 June 2026 and adds the active-business test, a limit to the police district where the labour-market test was done, and easier change of employer. Two details in the claim are wrong. The Croatian language exam is postponed to 4 June 2027. The 5,000-20,000 EUR fines were not verified; the fine I found for late notice to police is 660-920 EUR. Courts do prosecute these cases often. I found no Croatian product that tracks permits, but the core job (applying for permits) is done by the HZZ/MUP portal plus agencies and lawyers. That leaves a tracker for expiry dates and 15-day notices, which is close to generic HR software. Volume is high: 172,499 permits in 2024.

coverage.found: Zakon o vodi za ljudsku potrošnju (NN 30/23, in force 16.03.2023) defines mali isporučitelj (<10 m3/day or <50 persons, commercial or public activity). Duties: entry in the Ministry's electronic Registry of water suppliers via e-Građani (Art. 34; changes within 30 days, cessation within 8 days), self-funded monitoring of Group A and B parameters by official or authorised laboratories (Art. 48), 24-hour reporting of deviations to the sanitary inspectorate (Art. 32(6)). Art. 36: premises on their own water system or local waterworks (food processing, catering for 20 or more, camps, marinas, health and social facilities, and other commercial activity with more than 50 people) must test Group A four times a year and Group B every six years. Priority facilities need annual Legionella and lead monitoring (Art. 46). Fines EUR 3,980-13,270 for legal persons, EUR 660-1,320 for sole traders (Art. 71-72). Deadlines: large suppliers 1 Jan 2025; small suppliers 12 Jan 2029; priority facilities' risk assessment 31 Dec 2025. The Hrvatske vode '10 m3 or 50 people' note from the first pass is confirmed as the law's small-supplier threshold, not a Hrvatske vode register. Two weak candidates logged. Not read: Art. 36 original text, the monitoring rulebook with exact frequencies for small suppliers, and the last 28k characters of the law (zakon.hr).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Three regimes. (a) Private employment intermediaries (Zakon o tržištu rada, Art. 4): register with the labour ministry before starting, show the registration number on documents and ads, free to job seekers, send statistical data to the ministry (Art. 4(12)-(13)). (b) Temporary agencies (Zakon o radu Art. 44): registered and entered in the ministry's evidence, assign a worker to one user for at most a year, and deliver annual statistics on assigned workers under Pravilnik NN 98/2018 (previous 2015 text had a 1 March deadline; unconfirmed for the 2018 text). Roughly 752-921 agencies registered (one press figure, undated), 815 recorded in 2024 per Novi list. (c) Foreigners Act amendment NN 40/25 (in force 15 March 2025): labour market test by HZZ, promissory note (zadužnica) of EUR 1,821 per worker (MUP page, Oct 2025), guarantee of one average gross salary if the employer withdraws, changing employer after 6 months; agencies complain of 2-3 month permit delays. 41% of foreign workers in 2024 came through agencies, 98% of them third-country nationals. About 170,723 permits issued in 2025, 17% fewer than 2024. Worker-record rule: Pravilnik NN 55/24 requires employers to hold permit data per worker, in paper or electronic form. No Croatian permit-expiry tracker product found. Not checked: the agency-work rulebook on registration conditions and any guarantee, and the full penalties text.

result.competitor: The Ministry runs the database itself and issues access credentials (Art. 78(7),(10)), so a free state entry interface is likely. Its exact form (web form or API) was not found: the Ministry's instructions are not yet published. No Croatian vet practice-management software was found. Searches only turned up Anolla (a booking tool with treatment history) and foreign products (VetSet, Veti, ezyVet). None of them advertise integration with the Croatian database. Existing local vendors and any API are not verified.
result.duty: Confirmed in force. Zakon o veterinarskim lijekovima i veterinarskim medicinskim proizvodima, NN 69/2026, applies from 29 July 2026. Under Article 78(9), veterinarians must enter vaccination and treatment data into the Ministry's Nacionalna elektronička baza podataka za primjenu veterinarskih lijekova "u skladu s uputom Ministarstva". Point 1 (food-producing animals) takes effect 1.1.2027 and point 2 (non-food animals) 1.1.2029, per the transitional provisions. Wholesalers must record batch and expiry before a product goes on the market. Foreign vets need Ministry credentials. Entry is per treatment, so it is continuous. The fine for not entering data was not read: the penalty articles were not in the fetched text. The zakon.hr summary gives general fines for legal persons of EUR 10k-50k by severity.
result.market: Not found. No count from a register or statistic was reached. Companywall shows many registered "veterinarska ambulanta/stanica" companies (NKD 75.00), but no total was found. The 2027 wave covers only vets treating food-producing animals. Not reached: an HVK member register or a DZS count for NKD 75.00.
result.reason: The duty is real. Article 78(9) of NN 69/2026 makes vets enter vaccination and treatment records in the Ministry's national e-database, following Ministry instructions. This applies to food-producing animals from 1.1.2027 and to non-food animals from 1.1.2029. The State Inspectorate supervises it (Art. 7). No Croatian product was found that does this job. But the database is run by the Ministry, which hands out access credentials, so the state probably provides its own entry screen. Whether there is an API is unknown. That leaves only a 'double-entry avoidance' add-on, which depends on an interface that may not exist. The fine for non-entry was not read, and the number of practices was not found. Croatia's market is small, and the Ministry's instructions have not been published yet.

result.competitor: Six searches in Croatian and English found no named Croatian building-management or pričuva software. Results were law texts, DGU guidance, RRiF accounting articles, and unrelated tools: PlanRadar, Anolla, Schneider BMS, and BESTenergIS in Serbia. Vendors almost certainly exist, since managers have run pričuva bookkeeping for decades, but none were named in these results, so competition is unverified, not ruled out. The state side is DGU's OSS/ZIS portal, a free tool for entering register data; whether it accepts bulk import was not checked.
result.duty:
Confirmed in force: ZUOZ NN 152/24 (ispravak NN 47/26).
- Art. 61: new međuvlasnički ugovori and ugovori o upravljanju must be concluded within 2 years of entry into force, i.e. by 1.1.2027. Old contracts lapse then.
- Art. 60: registers set up within 6 months of entry into force.
- Art. 66: existing managers apply for RUZ/RZS within 6 months of the registers being set up (about 31.12.2025).
- Art. 10(3), 10(6), 12(3), 12(4): changes to register data within 15 or 8 days; register entry within 90 days of taking over a building.
- Art. 52: keep owner records up to date; annual report with itemised pričuva by February; annual programme by 15 Nov; multi-year programme by 31 Dec.
- Art. 29: minimum pričuva of 0.54% of the etalonska cijena per m2 per year.
- Art. 30: mandatory insurance of common parts.
- Art. 57: fines for an upravitelj legal entity €700 to €5,500, an individual €350 to €2,750, a responsible person €100 to €1,000, after a written warning from the komunalni redar.
- Art. 58: co-owners €1,000 to €10,000.
Filing is electronic only, via ZIS/OSS at DGU. Bulk upload was not verified: the DGU FAQ PDF could not be read.
result.market: Not found. DGU publishes no count of RUZ-registered upravitelji or RZS communities. Registry numbers run sequentially (RUZ1..n), but no total was found. Buildings number in the tens of thousands, but the buyers are a limited, concentrated set of management firms. That size is an estimate; no count was found.
result.reason: The duty is real. Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada (NN 152/24, corrected NN 47/26, in force since 1.1.2025) requires new co-owner and management contracts by 1.1.2027 (Art. 61), RZS/RUZ entry and updates within 8 to 15 days, and annual pričuva reports by February. Managers face fines of €700 to €5,500 after a written warning. But the register job was mostly one-off: the entry deadline passed around 31.12.2025, and the contract deadline is also one-off. The recurring part is general pričuva bookkeeping, which established Croatian manager packages probably already cover. Six searches found no named vendor, but they don't rule vendors out. The number of upravitelji isn't published. The firms are already consolidated, so the buyer pool is small and distribution is narrow.

result.competitor: AGRONET (APPRRR, free) already handles declarations, vineyard register changes and e-accompanying documents, so most of the claimed kit is covered by the state. Nothing found for the cellar book (Obrazac 3) in Croatia. Foreign or general products found: EOS WineSuite (Italy, Dynamics 365 based; covers cellar, transport documents and telematic registers, but not shown to be adapted to Croatia) and eVineyard (vineyard management, not cellar records). Slovenian or German cellar-book vendors in Croatia: not found.
result.duty: Pravilnik o vinarstvu NN 81/2022 (consolidated up to NN 75/2023 and later) replaced NN 48/14 under its Article 56. Article 7 sets the declarations, which are filed with APPRRR through AGRONET: harvest declaration (A1/A2) by 15 January, expected harvest declaration (protected-designation wines) by 31 July, production declaration (A3-A5) by 15 January, and stock declaration (as of 31 July) by 10 September. Exemptions: all grapes delivered to a winery, or family use under 10 hl. Under Articles 8-10, each consignment needs a prateći dokument requested and confirmed electronically in AGRONET. Under Article 43 (with Wine Act NN 32/19, Article 62(4)), the cellar book (podrumska evidencija) is kept on Obrazac 3, with entries within 3 days of each operation. Wine Act penalty amounts: not found.
result.market: APPRRR data at 31 December 2017: 39,014 farms with vineyards and 23,919 entered in the Vinogradarski registar. For the 2017 wine year, 3,729 farms filed mandatory grape and wine declarations; this is the best proxy for buyers who would need the cellar book. No current figure found.
result.reason: The duty is real, but the claim cites a repealed rulebook. Article 56 of Pravilnik o vinarstvu (NN 81/2022, consolidated text on zakon.hr) repeals NN 48/14. The free state tool AGRONET already handles the declarations and accompanying documents: harvest and production declarations are due 15 January, expected harvest 31 July and stock 10 September. Only the cellar book (Obrazac 3, entries within 3 days) seems to be kept outside AGRONET. No Croatian cellar-book product was found, only Italy's EOS WineSuite. Wine Act fines were not found. Market numbers are old: 3,729 farms filed declarations in 2017. Gap: a cellar-book app only, for micro wineries with low willingness to pay.

The duty is real. The amending act (NN 77/2026, in force 23 July 2026) requires a permit per vehicle, special plates, and the operator checking the AKD driver card by QR. Platforms must keep registers (6-month deadline), and municipalities must align by 31 March 2027. Operators already must keep an electronic vehicle register and report changes within 8 days. The NN text itself returned 503, so I used zakon.hr and secondary summaries. The duty is thin and mostly one-off: a free QR check, a small register, and permit renewals that cost about 93 EUR. Fines of 1,980-6,630 EUR for a missing card fall on the responsible person. No Croatian taxi compliance software turned up, but only generic dispatch tools were found. The market is small and fragmented, and willingness to pay is low. Operator count not found.

Duty is real: new Zakon o deviznom poslovanju (NN 27/26, in force 26.3.2026) requires a certified programme for all exchange transactions, reversals and cash changes, plus a quarterly report to HNB by the 10th of the next month. Fee and card-exchange rules apply from 26.12.2026. Penalties were not found. HNB ran a consultation on a new certified-programme decision (to 27.4.2026) and no final adoption was found. The market is tiny and gated: HNB certifies programmes and keeps a register of vendors, and a 2019 note suggests one vendor existed then. Vendor names and exchange-office count were not retrieved. A solo founder would need HNB certification, and the buyer pool is small. Weak opportunity.

The duty is real: NN 55/26 (published 27 May 2026) took effect 4 June 2026. The language exam applies from 4 June 2027, and old permits stay valid until they expire. I could not verify the police-district limit, board-member permits, the fine amounts or the A1.1 level in the pages I opened; the TEB page does not cover them. Two searches found no Croatian permit-tracking product, only legal explainers, and HZZ offers a state application for seasonal permits. The core job is mostly one-off permit applications by small employers, not a recurring filing, so frequency is weak. Employers can use generic HR tools and accountants, and law changes mean the product would need constant updating. Market size is not quantified. Score is low to moderate.

The EU duty is real (Reg. 2023/1115 as amended by 2025/2650). Application dates are 30 Dec 2026 for medium and large firms and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small. Sources conflict on whether micro and small firms already covered by the old EU Timber Regulation (EUTR) start on the earlier date, so I could not settle the timber date. Downstream traders mostly need to keep supplier and customer records and reference numbers for 5 years. I found no Croatian implementing law and no Croatian-language product. A FSC Adria document from 2024 names the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition as coordinator. The market is small, and the duty is light for downstream traders, who need little beyond record-keeping. Generic EUDR platforms (Coolset, Tracextech, osapiens) exist. Croatian wood-trader counts were not found. The Commission's 30 April 2026 simplification review outcome was not checked.

Duty is real and in force (NN 30/23, in force from 16.03.2023). Art. 36 requires campsites, marinas, social-care and health facilities serving 20 or more people to test Group A four times a year and Group B every six years. Food businesses must test Group A once a year. Small suppliers must monitor under Art. 48 and register under Art. 34. Fines are EUR 6,630-13,270 for legal persons (Art. 71) and EUR 3,980-9,290 for suppliers (Art. 72). I did not confirm that Art. 36 applies only to own-source premises, and Art. 46 sets Legionella and lead monitoring for priority facilities at least once a year. No dedicated Croatian water-monitoring scheduler was found. DHM (Digital HACCP Manager) is a general HACCP app, and I found nothing on its water-test features. Weaknesses: a small niche, labs already do the sampling, buyers pay little for reminders, and it would likely be a HACCP add-on. I did not check the market size, the Art. 81-82 text, or the Art. 34 registry's applicability to premises.
